data.raw_text:
Here's a repost of that interesting take on being stuck in traffic in Quezon City, written by GMA7 reporter Bernadette Reyes, who crawled to her destination for more than 4 hours (that's really miserable, considering the A-to-B distance), attributing her ordeal (with a tongue-in-cheek prologue) to the urban flooding in this rainy season:

hindi naman po sa pagyayabang ano? after more than 4 hours nakarating na kami from commonwealth to GMA Kamuning area 😄

mga realizations habang nasa stand still na traffic: 

hindi ko alam na parehas lang pala ang byahe ng commonwealth to GMA Kamuning at Philippines to Japan 😀 sa tindi ng traffic nakabalik na sana ako ng Japan 😅

buti hindi ako uminom ng maraming tubig

buti hindi ako uminom ng coffee with milk bilang lactose intolerant ako 

naging mas patient ako na tao 😀 

naisip ko yung ambulance na nag wawang-wang sa likod 🥹 sana okay lang ang pasyente 

buti marunong ako mag motor pero hindi ako nakamotor kanina 😀

on a more serious note, 
we need more drainage sa urban areas para bumababa ang tubig kahit bumubuhos ang ulan 

we need more discipline kasi yung ibang drainage nababarahan ng basura kaya lalong bumabagal ang pag baba bg tubig. 

lets not keep on changing lanes kapag ganitong stand still, the more we change lanes the more traffic we cause 

lets keep our heads cool. kapag nag kasagian pa lalong tatagal at hahaba ang traffic

wala pang bagyo yan ha, ganyan na kalala. paano pa pag bumabagyo na 🥹

kayo anong mga realization nyo habang nasa traffic? 😀

https://t.co/BeRvGDvAQh
